title: Ball strikes an outside influence
question: Suppose your ball accidentally strikes a dog running across the course. What does the Rule say you must do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies, with no penalty.
Replay the shot and add a penalty.
Drop a ball within two club lengths of where it hit the dog.

explanation: If your ball in motion hits an outside influence such as a dog, you must play your ball as it lies with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Your Ball Hits a Dog on the Golf Course
juniorVersion.question: If you hit the ball and it accidentally hits a dog running across the grass, what should you do next?

choices.text: Play the ball where it stops. There is no penalty.
Hit the shot again and add a penalty.
Drop the ball within two club lengths of where it hit the dog.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball hits something like a dog on the course, just play your ball where it lands. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A penalty means you have to add extra shots to your score because of breaking a rule.
Something or someone not part of your game, like a dog or a bird, that can change where your ball goes.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind children that sometimes things happen by accident on the course. The rules help keep the game fair and fun.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think they have to replay the shot or drop a new ball.
Some might think there is a penalty for hitting an animal, but there is not for this rule.
